item.title: Supply-chain attack using invisible code hits GitHub and other repositories
item.description:
📝 They usually work by uploading malicious packages with code and names that closely resemble those of widely used code libraries, with the objective of tricking developers into mistakenly incorporating the former into their software. Decoders see executable code The packages Aikido found this month have adopted a newer technique: selective use of code that isn’t visible when loaded into virtually all editors, terminals, and code review interfaces. To a JavaScript interpreter, the code points translate into executable code.
🔗 Read more: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/03/supply-chain-attack-using-invisible-code-hits-github-and-other-repositories/
